connotation.tone: The purpose holds against something that might have cowed it - it implies the attempt was made and failed.

family.axis: not easily moved from a purpose → immovably fixed on it whatever the cost

senses.definition: resolutely courageous

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Courage defined by what failed to stop it.

examples: undaunted in the face of death

family.axis: steady → heroic

senses.definition: not defended or capable of being defended

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Puts the weight on impossibility - not that defences are absent but that none could be made to hold.

family.axis: open to attack in principle → already taking the attack

senses.definition: not defended or capable of being defended

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Bare report of an absence, with no claim that defence was tried or that it could have worked.

family.axis: open to attack in principle → already taking the attack

senses.definition: subjected to enemy attack or censure

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Shifts from susceptibility to fact - the blows are landing, and they can be censure as readily as weapons.

family.axis: open to attack in principle → already taking the attack

senses.definition: subjected to enemy attack or censure

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: The vivid twin of *under attack*, its gunfire image carrying the same double reach over assault and criticism.

examples: an official under fire for mismanagement

family.axis: open to attack in principle → already taking the attack

senses.definition: not derivative or imitative

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Praise made by subtraction: it clears a thing of owing itself to a source and of copying a model, without claiming freshness the way *original* does.

examples: a natural underivative poet

family.axis: not copied from a model → unprecedented enough to found what follows

senses.definition: in the nature of something though not readily apparent

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Puts the sense beneath a surface rather than inside a nature, implying something could be uncovered, where *inherent* makes it permanent.

examples: an underlying meaning

family.axis: simply not put into words → lodged in the nature of the thing itself

senses.definition: located beneath or below
being or involving basic facts or principles
examples: underlying principles

senses.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Measures the people present against the strength the work was meant to have, framing the gap as a post held by too few.

family.axis: a shortfall merely counted → a fitness condemned

senses.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: The flattest of the four - a headcount below requirement, without the felt pressure of *short-handed*.

examples: overcrowded and understaffed hospitals

family.axis: a shortfall merely counted → a fitness condemned

senses.definition: know and comprehend the nature or meaning of
examples: She did not understand her husband
I understand what she means
the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character
senses.learner: to know what someone or something is really like, or what it means.

senses.definition: perceive (an idea or situation) mentally
examples: I don't understand the idea
Elizabeth soon observed, and instantly understood it.
senses.learner: to take in an idea or a situation in your mind.

senses.definition: make sense of a language
believe to be the case

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Softer than *believe*: it presents the belief as settled information one has come by, which lets the speaker hold it lightly.

examples: I understand you have no previous experience?
I understood that there were some very strong objections against the lady.
senses.learner: to believe that something is true.

family.axis: reasoned assent → uncritical credulity

senses.definition: be understanding of
examples: You don't need to explain — I understand!

senses.definition: characterized by understanding based on comprehension and discernment and empathy
examples: an understanding friend

senses.definition: the cognitive condition of someone who understands
examples: he has virtually no understanding of social cause and effect
She had almost no understanding of how the money was to be shared out.
senses.learner: the state of mind of a person who understands something.

senses.definition: the statement (oral or written) of an exchange of promises
examples: there was an understanding between management and the workers
before you take any, or all of these houses, for your son and daughter, let us come to a right understanding
senses.learner: a spoken or written statement of the promises two sides have traded.

senses.definition: an inclination to support or be loyal to or to agree with an opinion
examples: I knew I could count on his understanding

senses.definition: the capacity for rational thought or inference or discrimination
senses.learner: the power to think clearly, to work things out, and to tell things apart.
examples: She was a woman of mean understanding, little information, and uncertain temper.
Her understanding excellent, her mind improved, and her manners captivating.

senses.definition: fully apprehended as to purport or meaning or explanation
examples: the understood conditions of troop withdrawal were clear

senses.definition: implied by or inferred from actions or statements

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Adds successful uptake: the meaning was not merely implied but taken up on both sides, where *tacit* says only that it went unsaid.

examples: the understood provisos of a custody agreement

family.axis: simply not put into words → lodged in the nature of the thing itself

senses.definition: being very thin

connotation.label: negative
connotation.explanation: States a fact about weight, but names it as a shortfall.
connotation.tone: Measured against a medical standard rather than an opinion - the neutral clinical term.

family.axis: condemning → praising

senses.definition: going directly ahead from one point to another without veering or turning aside
examples: some people see evolution as an undeviating upward march from simple organisms to the very complex

senses.definition: used of values and principles; not subject to change; steady

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Steadiness treated as a virtue of principle, praising what refuses to bend.

examples: undeviating loyalty

family.axis: trusted → proven by use

senses.definition: plain to see

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Names concealment in order to deny it, so what is plain to see carries the sense of something that could have been hidden and was not.

examples: undisguised curiosity

family.axis: merely observable → unconcealed to the point of effrontery

senses.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Defined by what it withholds, measuring out its approval as an absence of rigidity rather than any positive warmth.

family.axis: quiet readiness to hear a new idea → outright refusal of authority and dogma

senses.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: The longer, stiffer twin of *undogmatic*, its extra syllable pulling it further from anything conversational.

family.axis: quiet readiness to hear a new idea → outright refusal of authority and dogma

senses.definition: not domesticated

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: A flat negation and nothing more, the plainest term in the family, with none of the menace *feral* adds.

examples: a few undomesticated horses left

family.axis: plainly untamed → untamed and threatening

senses.definition: unaccustomed to home life
examples: after years of marriage he remained essentially undomesticated

senses.definition: not done
examples: the work could be done or undone and nobody cared

senses.definition: doomed to extinction

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Formal and near-elegiac, treating the end as something that came apart rather than something that was smashed.

family.axis: a bare failed outcome → finished, with nothing left and nothing coming

senses.definition: not fastened or tied or secured
examples: her blouse had come undone at the neck
his shoelaces were undone

senses.definition: thrown into a state of disorganization or incoherence

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Sounds the same collapse as an unmaking, graver and more final than *unstuck* - the thing not merely loosened but ruined.

family.axis: merely unmethodical → snarled into total wreckage

senses.definition: without doubt; certainly
examples: it's undoubtedly very beautiful
Bingley likes your sister undoubtedly; but he may never do more than like her, if she does not help him on.
You think it a faithful portrait, undoubtedly.
senses.learner: in a way that leaves no doubt; for certain

senses.definition: of lumber or stone or hides; not finished or dressed

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Names one specific operation left undone rather than a general falling-short, which keeps it cooler and more technical than *unfinished*.

examples: undressed granite
undressed hides

family.axis: neutral record of an unworked state → shortfall measured against the state wanted

senses.definition: having removed clothing
not yet payable
examples: an undue loan

senses.definition: not appropriate or proper (or even legal) in the circumstances
examples: undue influence
I didn't want to show undue excitement
accused of using undue force

senses.definition: lacking justification or authorization
examples: desire for undue private profit

senses.definition: beyond normal limits

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Faults the excess for not being warranted rather than for its bulk, the quietest complaint among the words sharing its gloss.

examples: his dress stops just short of undue elegance

family.axis: registering a degree past the norm → denouncing it as past all reason

senses.definition: lacking a sense of security or affording no ease or reassurance
examples: farmers were uneasy until rain finally came
uneasy about his health
gave an uneasy laugh
uneasy lies the head that wears the crown
an uneasy coalition government
an uneasy calm
an uneasy silence fell on the group

senses.definition: lacking or not affording physical or mental rest
examples: she fell into an uneasy sleep

senses.definition: causing or fraught with or showing anxiety
socially uncomfortable; unsure and constrained in manner
examples: was always uneasy with strangers

senses.definition: relating to bodily unease that causes discomfort

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The faintest of these: a bodily unsettledness that has not hardened into pain, more a hint than a hurt.

family.axis: faint bodily unease → outright physical misery

senses.definition: continuing forever or indefinitely

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Frames endlessness as the plain absence of a stop, without the grandeur *eternal* brings or the warmth of *everlasting*.

examples: the unending bliss of heaven

family.axis: lasts a long while → never ends

senses.definition: with unflagging resolve

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: The adverb of *unending*: frames endlessness as the plain absence of a stop, without the grandeur *eternal* brings or the warmth of *everlasting*.

family.axis: lasts a long while → never ends

senses.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The same limit measured in duration - what cannot be lasted out, where *unbearable* is what cannot be held up under.

family.axis: hard to bear → past all bearing or defending

senses.definition: not busy or occupied; free

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Purely factual: not currently occupied, with no view taken on why.

examples: the cancellation left her unengaged a good part of the afternoon

family.axis: accusing → enviable

senses.definition: not promised in marriage
examples: continued seeing him but on an unengaged basis

senses.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: An understated verdict that condemns by observation - the thing is framed as unwished-for, and the word damns it without raising its voice.

examples: in the unenviable position of resorting to an act he had planned to save for the climax of the campaign

family.axis: difficulty framed as a stretch worth making → difficulty framed as a predicament no one would want

senses.definition: so undesirable as to be incapable of arousing envy
examples: unenviable notoriety

senses.definition: poorly balanced or matched in quantity or value or measure

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Carries a fault inside the measurement - poorly balanced or matched, not merely different - where *nonequivalent* only records that the quantities fail to agree.

family.axis: neutral statement of non-equality → imbalance felt as a fault or unfairness

senses.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Weighs what is brought against what the task takes and finds the two mismatched, where *inadequate* names the shortfall as a defect in the thing itself.

examples: she was unequal to the task

family.axis: a shortfall merely counted → a fitness condemned

senses.definition: not meeting requirements

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The gentlest way of saying the requirement went unmet, setting the demand beside the resource and leaving the failure unassigned where *incompetent* pins it.

examples: unequal to the demands put upon him

family.axis: a shortfall merely counted → a fitness condemned

senses.definition: not caused to be equal

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: The British spelling of *unequalized* and just as unjudging - it says only that nothing was made equal.

family.axis: neutral statement of non-equality → imbalance felt as a fault or unfairness

senses.definition: not caused to be equal

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Points at what was not done rather than at the result: no levelling has been applied, where *unequal* passes judgement on the gap that remains.

family.axis: neutral statement of non-equality → imbalance felt as a fault or unfairness

senses.definition: in an unequal or partial manner

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The adverb of *unequal*: carries a fault inside the measurement - poorly balanced or matched, not merely different - where *nonequivalent* only records that the quantities fail to agree.

examples: angry at being dealt with so unequally

family.axis: neutral statement of non-equality → imbalance felt as a fault or unfairness

senses.definition: admitting of no doubt or misunderstanding; having only one meaning or interpretation and leading to only one conclusion
examples: unequivocal evidence
took an unequivocal position
an unequivocal success
an unequivocal promise
an unequivocal (or univocal) statement

senses.definition: clearly defined or formulated

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Defines by exclusion where *definitive* defines by settlement: the wording is clear because no second reading survives it.

examples: the plain and unequivocal language of the laws

family.axis: merely put into words → spelled out to the last unsoftened detail

senses.definition: not even or uniform as e.g. in shape or texture
examples: an uneven color
uneven ground
uneven margins
wood with an uneven grain

senses.definition: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Softer than *mismatched* for the same unfair contest: it notes that the thing tilts one way without condemning the making of the match.

examples: vaudeville … waged an uneven battle against the church

family.axis: neutral statement of non-equality → imbalance felt as a fault or unfairness

senses.definition: not divisible by two
variable and recurring at irregular intervals
examples: an uneven gait
uneven spacing

senses.definition: lacking consistency

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The mildest of these - it registers variation without deciding that any part of the thing has failed.

family.axis: bare failure to match → outright contradiction

senses.definition: in an uneven and irregular way
in a ragged uneven manner

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The adverb of *uneven*: the mildest of these - it registers variation without deciding that any part of the thing has failed.

family.axis: bare failure to match → outright contradiction

senses.definition: in an unequal or partial manner
examples: profits were distributed unevenly

senses.definition: not made explicit

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Neutral and general — it says the thing found no outward form at all, without insisting that words in particular were what went missing.

examples: the unexpressed terms of the agreement

family.axis: simply not put into words → lodged in the nature of the thing itself

senses.definition: not liable to failure
examples: the unfailing sign of an amateur
an unfailing test

senses.definition: always able to supply more
examples: an unfailing source of good stories
a subject of unfailing interest

senses.definition: tireless

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Approving of what never runs out, measuring steadiness by supply rather than by the refusal to vary that *constant* asks for.

examples: unfailing loyalty
unfailing good spirits

family.axis: unchanging as a bare fact → steadiness that never tires

senses.definition: not true to duty or obligation or promises
examples: an unfaithful lover

senses.definition: having sexual relations with someone other than your husband or wife, or your boyfriend or girlfriend
examples: her husband was unfaithful

senses.definition: having the character of, or characteristic of, a traitor
not trustworthy

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: A failure of trust rather than of aim - what it names has let someone down.

examples: an unfaithful reproduction

family.axis: slightly off → flatly wrong

senses.definition: of depth; not capable of being sounded or measured
resembling an abyss in depth; so deep as to be unmeasurable
incapable of being fully understood

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Depth is the image, and it grants that understanding goes some way down and simply never reaches the bottom.

family.axis: a difficulty the reader can work at → understanding shut out entirely

senses.definition: (of market animals) not optimal for marketing

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Coolly commercial disparagement - the animal is graded short of what the market wants, a deficiency stated as plain fact rather than complaint.

family.axis: neutral record of an unworked state → shortfall measured against the state wanted

senses.definition: not pretended; sincerely felt or expressed

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Defined against pretence, which is a curious way to have to say it.

examples: her interest in people was unfeigned

family.axis: polite formula → wholehearted

senses.definition: with sincerity; without pretense

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: The adverb of *unfeigned*: defined against pretence, which is a curious way to have to say it.

examples: was unfeignedly glad to see his old teacher

family.axis: polite formula → wholehearted

senses.definition: not brought to the desired final state

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Carries a faint reproach because the thing is measured against the final state that was wanted, so it records a shortfall rather than merely a stage.

family.axis: neutral record of an unworked state → shortfall measured against the state wanted

senses.definition: not brought to an end or conclusion
examples: unfinished business
the building is still unfinished

senses.definition: lacking a surface finish such as paint
examples: unfinished furniture

senses.definition: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Praises what does not happen - the enthusiasm never dips - so it commends steadiness where *tireless* commends capacity.

examples: unflagging pursuit of excellence

family.axis: energy simply present → energy that will not flag

senses.definition: tireless

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: The same tirelessness as *unfailing*, but figured as a pace that never slackens rather than a store that never empties.

examples: unflagging courtesy

family.axis: unchanging as a bare fact → steadiness that never tires

senses.definition: not easily perturbed or excited or upset; marked by extreme calm and composure

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: Informal and warmly admiring where *imperturbable* is dignified, praising the same immunity to upset in cheerful terms.

examples: unflappable in a crisis

family.axis: untroubled stillness → unshakeable command of oneself under pressure

senses.definition: without a flaw

connotation.label: positive
connotation.tone: The plain negation beside *flawless*, denying the flaw without carrying the admiration.

family.axis: no fault found in it → complete and consummate perfection

senses.definition: not favored by fortune; marked or accompanied by or resulting in ill fortune

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The mildest way to mark ill luck, registering that fortune went against someone with none of the ruin *calamitous* insists on.

examples: an unfortunate turn of events
an unfortunate decision
unfortunate investments
an unfortunate night for all concerned

family.axis: misfortune total enough to bring ruin or invite contempt → plain ill luck

senses.definition: not auspicious; boding ill
unsuitable or regrettable

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The gentlest wording available - it calls a thing unsuitable and regrettable at once, treating the fault as bad luck rather than bad work.

examples: an unfortunate choice of words
an unfortunate speech

family.axis: regrettably unsuitable → graceless to the point of incompetence

senses.definition: a person who suffers misfortune
by bad luck

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The adverb of *unfortunate*: the mildest way to mark ill luck, registering that fortune went against someone with none of the ruin *calamitous* insists on.

examples: unfortunately it rained all day

family.axis: misfortune total enough to bring ruin or invite contempt → plain ill luck

senses.definition: not related to or suitable for everyday needs or activities

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Carries no verdict at all - it records unsuitability for everyday needs where *impractical* implies a fault.

family.axis: unsuited to practical use → derided as senseless

senses.definition: lacking in magnanimity
examples: it seems ungenerous to end this review of a splendid work of scholarship on a critical note

senses.definition: unwilling to spend (money, time, resources, etc.)

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Names the missing virtue rather than the present vice, which makes it the politer complaint.

examples: an ungenerous response to the appeal for funds

family.axis: contemptible → merely careful

senses.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.

examples: ungodly acts

family.axis: merely liable to sin → wicked past any reform

senses.definition: worried and uneasy

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: The most detached way of naming the worried unease, stating it as a condition and holding nothing against the person in it.

family.axis: worried unease → discontent turned openly against authority

senses.definition: experiencing or marked by or causing sadness or sorrow or discontent
examples: unhappy over her departure
unhappy with her raise
after the argument they lapsed into an unhappy silence
had an unhappy time at school
the unhappy (or sad) news
he looks so unhappy
without scheming to do wrong, or to make others unhappy
I was uncomfortable enough, I was very uncomfortable--I may say unhappy.
senses.learner: feeling sadness, sorrow or discontent, showing it, or causing it.

senses.definition: generalized feeling of distress
senses.learner: having a general feeling of distress.
examples: He had been unhappy for weeks, without being able to say why.

senses.definition: causing discomfort
examples: the unhappy truth
Conceal the unhappy truth as long as it is possible.
senses.learner: making people feel uncomfortable.

senses.definition: marked by or producing unhappiness
examples: unhappy caravans, straggling afoot through swamps and canebrakes

senses.definition: disregarded

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The mildest of the three: it grants that something stood there to be attended to, without *ignored*'s deliberateness or *neglected*'s failure of care.

examples: his cries were unheeded

family.axis: bare absence of notice → attention withheld from something with a claim on it

senses.definition: providing no assistance

connotation.label: negative
connotation.explanation: Built from 'un-' negating a virtue - failing to give help that was looked for.

examples: The manual was unhelpful on this point.
an unhelpful reply that answered nothing

senses.definition: (of stone especially) not given a finished form by or as if by hewing

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Denies the shaping outright where *roughhewn* concedes a first pass, and its as-if reach lets it settle on things no tool was ever near.

examples: a house of unhewn grey stone roughly cemented together

family.axis: neutral record of an unworked state → shortfall measured against the state wanted

senses.definition: showing utter resignation or hopelessness

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: A bare negation covering the same utter resignation or hopelessness as *abject*, but with the contempt drained out and understatement left to carry it.

family.axis: faint hope still left → hope wholly gone and the collapse showing

senses.definition: deficient in originality or creativity; lacking powers of invention
examples: unimaginative development of a musical theme

senses.definition: dealing only with concrete facts
lacking spontaneity or originality or individuality

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The plainest naming of the deficit, no slang and no figure, just the absence stated as the fault.

examples: even his profanity was unimaginative

family.axis: flat naming of dullness → slangy contempt for rigid, predictable sameness

senses.definition: poorly articulated or enunciated, or drowned by noise
examples: unintelligible speech

senses.definition: hard or impossible to understand

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Blunt where *opaque* is figurative, and it reaches the same distance: from hard to make out to not to be made out at all.

family.axis: a difficulty the reader can work at → understanding shut out entirely

senses.definition: act in concert or unite in a common purpose or belief
senses.learner: to act together with others, or to come together in a shared aim or belief
examples: Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia
The united efforts of his two unfeeling sisters, and of his overpowering friend

senses.definition: become one
have or possess in combination
be or become joined or united or linked
senses.learner: to be joined to something else, or to become joined or linked to it
examples: Miss Elizabeth Bennet would, in all likelihood, be soon afterwards united to my nephew

senses.definition: bring together for a common purpose or action or ideology or in a shared situation
join or combine
senses.learner: to join things together, or to put them together into one
examples: Elizabeth tried to unite civility and truth in a few short sentences.

senses.definition: without substance

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: A plain report of the shortfall, measuring the thing against life and finding it thin, with none of *cardboard*'s contempt.

family.axis: plainly made rather than natural → so made it has no substance behind it

senses.definition: having no limits in range or scope
examples: to start with a theory of unlimited freedom is to end up with unlimited despotism

senses.definition: without reservation or exception

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Reads as sheer extent — nothing bounds the thing — where *outright* reads as manner, nothing qualifying it.

family.axis: bare report that nothing limits it → emphatic refusal to admit any reservation or exception

senses.definition: that cannot be entirely consumed or used up
having nothing extraneous

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Flatter than *uncluttered* - it denies mess rather than paying a compliment for its absence.

examples: the unlittered shoulders of the road

family.axis: bare absence of mess → admiring, kept-up order

senses.definition: without beauty or charm

connotation.label: negative
connotation.explanation: The gentlest way to say it.
connotation.tone: Understated - withholds beauty rather than asserting ugliness.

family.axis: cruellest → mildest

senses.definition: having or bringing misfortune
examples: Friday the 13th is an unlucky date
He has been so unlucky as to lose your friendship.
I am particularly unlucky in meeting with a person so well able to expose my real character.
senses.learner: Having bad luck, or bringing bad luck.

senses.definition: marked by or promising bad fortune
examples: the unlucky prisoner was again put in irons
The unlucky ship sailed out that morning and was never seen again.
senses.learner: Showing bad fortune, or promising bad fortune to come.

senses.definition: not having an identifying mark
examples: unmarked cards
an unmarked police car

senses.definition: not taken into account

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Flat where *overlooked* is apologetic: it says only that nothing was made of the thing, conceding no mistake.

examples: his retirement was not allowed to go unmarked

family.axis: bare absence of notice → attention withheld from something with a claim on it

senses.definition: without meaning

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: The plainest statement in the family, that meaning is simply absent, with none of the scorn *vacuous* or *nonsensical* carry.

examples: Silence is better than unmeaning words
an unmeaning smile

family.axis: flat statement that meaning is absent → contemptuous dismissal of a thing as void of it

senses.definition: having or showing no mercy

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: Mercy named only as the thing withheld - slightly more formal than 'merciless'.

family.axis: annihilating → merely unrelenting

senses.definition: without pity; in a merciless manner

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The adverb of *unmerciful*: mercy named only as the thing withheld - slightly more formal than 'merciless'.

family.axis: annihilating → merely unrelenting

senses.definition: not efficient or methodical

connotation.label: negative
connotation.tone: The coolest reproach here - it faults the missing method and the inefficiency that comes with it, and pictures no wreckage at all.

examples: the project failed through unmethodical planning

family.axis: merely unmethodical → snarled into total wreckage

senses.definition: not mixed with extraneous elements

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Formal and slightly stiff, denying admixture in so many words rather than asserting purity outright as *pure* does.

family.axis: unmixed as a bare fact → purity admired as flawlessness

senses.definition: clearly evident to the mind

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Force without approval - it makes clarity a matter of no other reading being available, which serves the unwelcome as readily as the welcome.

examples: his opposition to slavery was unmistakable

family.axis: obviousness held against a thing → clarity counted to its credit

senses.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

connotation.label: neutral
connotation.tone: Works by ruling out the alternative: the thing cannot be read as anything else, a firmer guarantee than *apparent* gives.

family.axis: easy to see → so complete it needs no proof or explanation
